items.originalTitle: SEALSQ Unveils VaultIC409 Secure Element for Post-Quantum Cryptography
items.summary: Insider Brief SEALSQ has unveiled VaultIC409, a secure element built on its QS7001 platform to support post-quantum cryptography in connected devices without requiring customers to redesign their existing hardware security architecture. VaultIC409 is designed to support ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), RSA and ECC, with a hardware Root of Trust, dedicated cryptographic acceleration and SPI connectivity.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief SEALSQ has unveiled VaultIC409, a secure element built on its QS7001 platform to support post-quantum cryptography in connected devices without requiring customers to redesign their existing hardware security architecture.
VaultIC409 is designed to support ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), RSA and ECC, with a hardware Root of Trust, dedicated cryptographic acceleration and SPI connectivity.

SEALSQ plans to demonstrate VaultIC409 using a TLS 1.3 application at Electronica from November 10–13, 2026, with engineering samples expected in Q2 2027; the underlying QS7001 platform is undergoing Common Criteria EAL5+ certification.

PRESS RELEASE — SEALSQ Corp (NASDAQ: LAES) (“SEALSQ” or “Company”), a company that focuses on developing and selling Semiconductors, PKI, and Post-Quantum technology hardware and software products, today unveils VaultIC409, a next-generation secure element designed to help hardware manufacturers address the growing cybersecurity challenges posed by quantum computing.

Built on SEALSQ’s QS7001 platform, which is currently undergoing Common Criteria EAL5+ certification process, VaultIC409 targets the same established markets as VaultIC408, giving existing customers a path to post-quantum security without redesigning their hardware security foundation.

VaultIC409 combines a hardware-based Root of Trust, cryptographic agility, dedicated cryptographic acceleration and Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) connectivity to provide a scalable foundation for the next generation of secure connected devices.
VaultIC409 gives our customers a direct path to post-quantum security on a certified platform they already know,” said Carlos Moreira, Founder and CEO of SEALSQ .

Extending our VaultIC family positions SEALSQ to support that transition across smart energy, industrial and IoT markets.” Demonstration and Availability SEALSQ plans to demonstrate VaultIC409’s capabilities through a TLS 1.3 application on its booth at the Electronica trade show (Hall C6 – 670) November 10 – 13, showcasing how hardware-based security, cryptographic acceleration and secure connectivity can support next-generation connected devices.
Engineering samples of VaultIC409 are planned to become available in Q2 2027, enabling customers and partners to evaluate the solution and begin integration activities for future product designs.

With VaultIC409, we are bringing together cryptographic agility, dedicated hardware acceleration and SPI connectivity to address the practical challenges of deploying Post-Quantum Cryptography in embedded devices,” said Gweltas Radenac, Product Marketing Director at SEALSQ .

“The ability to support RSA, ECC and PQC algorithms, combined with a hardware platform undergoing Common Criteria EAL5+ certification, gives manufacturers a foundation to provision identities, establish secure channels and anchor trust at runtime while preparing their products for the quantum era.” Built for Quantum-Safe Trust VaultIC409 extends SEALSQ ‘s VaultIC secure element portfolio with a security architecture designed for the transition toward quantum-resistant cryptography.

The secure element is designed to support emerging Post-Quantum Cryptography standards, including ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for quantum-resistant key establishment and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for digital signatures, alongside established cryptographic mechanisms required for hybrid security architectures.

evidenceRecords.text: Researchers at KAIST, TDS Innovation, Hanyang University, UNIST , et al. published a technical paper titled “Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux.” Abstract Excerpt: “Nucleation control is fundamental to semiconductor deposition, governing when, where and how crystalline materials form.
Conventional strategies can regulate nucleation density and, through area-selective growth, confine deposition to designated regions.

However, they generally do not determine where an individual nucleus forms within the growth regions, leaving even single-nucleation events spatially stochastic and limiting deterministic construction of crystalline materials.
Here we report etching-flux-mediated single-centred nucleation of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors to deterministically localize a single nucleation event.” Find the technical paper here .

items.title: FN America unveils M240 upgrade kit for modern optics
items.originalTitle: FN America unveils M240 upgrade kit for modern optics
items.summary: FN America introduced a new upgrade kit for the M240 machine gun on Monday at the annual meeting of the Association of the United States Army, giving soldiers a way to mount modern optics on the legacy platform. “With this upgrade kit, modern warfighters can achieve faster target acquisition, more consistent shooter fit and better management of optics, while military organizations can extend the value and relevance of currently fielded platforms,” Atkins said. The Army and Marine Corps are also pursuing separate efforts to modernize their squad-level weapons.

evidenceRecords.text: FN America introduced a new upgrade kit for the M240 machine gun on Monday at the annual meeting of the Association of the United States Army, giving soldiers a way to mount modern optics on the legacy platform.

In a press release, Daryl Atkins, FN’s director for industrialized weapons, said the M240 Tactical Long Rail Upgrade Kit will allow military organizations to continue “taking advantage of the weapon’s proven performance while making it relevant for today’s combat requirements.” According to the company, the kit preserves the weapon’s original operating system and can be installed on new guns or used to upgrade existing weapons.

The kit includes: An 11-inch monolithic Picatinny top rail to accommodate night-vision and thermal optics, along with other components; An FN Side-Click feed cover designed to make one-handed operation easier; An FN Auto-Lock feed cover retention system that holds the cover open during loading, unloading and cleaning; A long, articulated carrying handle designed to accommodate full-size optics; An adjustable buttstock that allows soldiers to change the length of pull and cheek height or fold the stock for storage.

“With this upgrade kit, modern warfighters can achieve faster target acquisition, more consistent shooter fit and better management of optics, while military organizations can extend the value and relevance of currently fielded platforms,” Atkins said.

FN, the Belgian firearms manufacturer with operations in Virginia and South Carolina, has produced more than 100,000 M240 machine guns for the U.S. military since the 7.62mm weapon entered service in 1977.
However, last year the Army revealed through budget documents that it was investing $3.6 billion in a project, dubbed the Future Medium Machine Gun, or FMMG, to replace the legacy system.
The Army and Marine Corps are also pursuing separate efforts to modernize their squad-level weapons.

items.originalTitle: Amid unease in Europe, NATO SACEUR bullish on ‘block, blunt, break’ theory of victory
items.summary: BELFAST — Despite assuring an audience today that a conflict on NATO territory is neither “imminent or inevitable,” Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, the alliance’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, outlined a strategic “theory of victory” and offered a warning to potential aggressors. NATO is capable of carrying out this vision by implementing its “theory of victory,” a classified version of which was agreed upon by all 32 alliance members “about three months ago,” according to Grynkewich.

evidenceRecords.text: BELFAST — Despite assuring an audience today that a conflict on NATO territory is neither “imminent or inevitable,” Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, the alliance’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, outlined a strategic “theory of victory” and offered a warning to potential aggressors.

NATO is capable of carrying out this vision by implementing its “theory of victory,” a classified version of which was agreed upon by all 32 alliance members “about three months ago,” according to Grynkewich.

Grynkewich, who also serves as commander of United States European Command, did not say against whom, exactly, the alliance would fight, but the speech comes as European capitals have increasingly called out Russia for what they alleged are a string of sabotage cases across the continent.
Grynkewich said the incidents were making allied populations “a bit nervous.”
Grynkewich warned, “I want others to know who might be thinking about doing harm against us, that we’ve got this, and that they better not take any shot at the alliance.”
The theory of victory is structured around blocking, blunting and breaking an enemy — beginning with stymieing an initial attack and preventing an enemy advance by weakening it.
